name: Question 8
problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis in the direction of increasing $x,$ away from a fixed origin $O.$ When the displacement of $P$ from $O$ is $x\,m,$ its velocity is $v\,m/s$ and its acceleration is $(2+3{e}^{-x})\,{m/s}^{2}.$ If $v=2\,m/s$ when $x=0\,\text{m},$ find the velocity of $P$ when $x=3\,\text{m}.$ Round your answer to one decimal place.
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14041958/assets/ec4af1357e75dcee6d7d5412467c2ee2ea9e54fa38fb6e83817b0ae909c529aa.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ is $(2+3{e}^{-x})\,{m/s}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=2+3{e}^{-x}.
$$

Using the fact that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=2+3{e}^{-x}.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int (2+3{e}^{-x})\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=2x-3{e}^{-x}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=2\,\text{m/s}$ when $x=0\,\text{m},$ we can find the value of the constant $C$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}(2)^{2} & =2(0)-3{e}^{-0}+C \\ 2 & =-3+C \\ C & =2+3 \\ C & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =2x-3{e}^{-x}+5 \\ {v}^{2} & =4x-6{e}^{-x}+10 \\ v & =\pm \sqrt{4x-6{e}^{-x}+10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the particle is moving in the direction of increasing $x,$ we have that $v(x)>0,$ so we can discard the negative square root. Therefore,

$$
v=\sqrt{4x-6{e}^{-x}+10}.
$$

Finally, the velocity of $P$ at $x=3$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\sqrt{4(3)-6{e}^{-3}+10} \\ v & =\sqrt{22-6{e}^{-3}} \\ v & ≈4.7\,\text{m/s},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.

Question 8
?

A particle P moves along the x-axis in the direction of increasing x, away from a fixed origin O. When the displacement of P from O is xm, its velocity is vm/s and its acceleration is (2+3e−x)m/s2. If v=2m/s when x=0m, find the velocity of P when x=3m. Round your answer to one decimal place.

a
 4.2 m/s
b
 3.8 m/s
c
 3.4 m/s
d
 4.7 m/s
e
 5.1 m/s
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since the acceleration of the particle P is (2+3e−x)m/s2, we have dvdt=2+3e−x.

Using the fact that

dvdt=ddx(12v2)

we can rewrite our equation as

ddx(12v2)=2+3e−x.

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to x, we have

∫ddx(12v2)dx=∫(2+3e−x)dx

which gives the general solution

12v2=2x−3e−x+C.

Now, since v=2m/s when x=0m, we can find the value of the constant C, as follows:

12(2)2=2(0)−3e−0+C2=−3+CC=2+3C=5

Therefore,

12v2=2x−3e−x+5v2=4x−6e−x+10v=±4x−6e−x+10.

Since the particle is moving in the direction of increasing x, we have that v(x)>0, so we can discard the negative square root. Therefore, v=4x−6e−x+10.

Finally, the velocity of P at x=3 is given by v=4(3)−6e−3+10v=22−6e−3v≈4.7m/s, rounded to one decimal place.
